name: Zara Barclay
life: “I still remember finishing restaurant prep before my own child's alarm.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Zara by a small Monday habit. Zara checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I love feeding strangers. I don't want my children to think that's easier than feeding them.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for an unlined tan jacket and a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. Zara has a round face with a pronounced chin, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Zara leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Zara has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To find one weekly breakfast at home with the teenagers.
family: Orla Till is Zara’s second cousin. Zara can always ask for five minutes alone. Orla asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The porch light*, Orla says, “I used the lamp to know exactly how far I had left to walk.”
connections: Anita Porter (daughter). The cook and the oldest child finally talk about who has been making breakfast at home.

reactions.response: Zara checks what the earlier start would do to the cook's family breakfast.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Zara brings the envelope to the counter unopened and stays long enough to make a note of who accepted it.
